one_liner: Header-only C++14 constexpr immutable set/map/unordered_map built on compile-time perfect hashing; beats std::unordered_map on fixed key sets.
what_it_does: Frozen provides immutable, constexpr-constructible versions of std::set, std::map, std::unordered_set and std::unordered_map, plus constexpr Boyer-Moore and KMP searchers, for key sets known at compile time. The element count is part of the type (frozen::unordered_map<K, V, N>, or let make_unordered_map deduce it). There is no insert, erase or operator[]; lookups use find/at/count/contains/equal_range. A constexpr instance fixes keys and values and folds lookups on constant keys at compile time. A non-constexpr instance (ideally constinit) keeps the keys fixed but lets you write values through at() or find().
how_it_is_fast: unordered_* uses a two-level perfect hash (not minimal) in the hash-and-displace style of Steve Hanov's 'Throw away the keys', built entirely in constexpr. Keys are seed-hashed into M buckets, where M is the next power of two at or above N (doubled below 32 keys). Buckets are processed largest first. A singleton bucket stores its item index directly in table G. A larger bucket gets a per-bucket seed, found by random search with minstd_rand, that puts all its items into free slots of table H. A lookup is one hash into G, at most one more seeded hash into H, then a single key comparison: no probing, no chains, no heap. frozen::set and frozen::map are sorted arrays searched by a fully unrolled branchless binary search.
when_to_use: Lookup tables whose key set is fixed at build time: keyword/command/opcode dispatch, enum<->string, symbol tables, HTML entities (all shipped as examples). Tens to a few thousand keys.
You need lookups in constant expressions (static_assert, template arguments, constexpr functions), or want constant-key lookups folded away entirely.

You want no static-initialization cost and no heap: declare constexpr or constinit and the table goes into the binary. FROZEN_NO_EXCEPTIONS (or -fno-exceptions) turns at()'s throw into std::abort for embedded builds.
Keys are fixed but values change at runtime, like the preprint's 4,042-key ticker->price table (~1.34x vs std::unordered_map). Use a constinit map and write through at() or find()->second.
Ordered lookups (lower_bound/upper_bound, sorted iteration) over immutable data, where frozen::map/set replace a node-based std::map/std::set with a sorted array.
when_not_to_use: Keys are only known at runtime, or the set changes: there is no insert, erase or rehash. Use a runtime hash map, or a runtime-built PHF such as fph-table or cmph.

Large key sets. In the preprint, frozen took 21.1 s to compile the 4,042-key demo vs 1.5 s for std::unordered_map. Big tables hit constexpr step limits (-fconstexpr-steps / -fconstexpr-ops-limit), and issue #76 (open) reports VS2017 failing at 500 entries.

Raw lookup throughput is the goal. static_maps ran at 45-97% of frozen's time in the same preprint, and the ConstexprCore/perfect_hash benchmark shows frozen::unordered_map at 0.16 vs 1.08 billion queries/s.
Long string keys on a hot path. The default string hash is a byte-at-a-time FNV-1a-style loop and can run twice per lookup (G then H), so cost grows with key length.
MSVC with warnings-as-errors: the constexpr hash triggers C4307 'integral constant overflow' warnings (#68, #178). Also, wasm32 has an open, unreproduced report of failed lookups (#198).

integration.min_toolchain: C++14. README: Clang 5+, GCC 6+ (slow constexpr), VS2017; GCC 5 unsupported. CI builds GCC 10-13, Clang 13/14/16, AppleClang and MSVC at C++14/17/2a. std::string_view keys need C++17, constinit needs C++20. CMake 3.10+ for the optional install/find_package path.
integration.platforms: any (portable C++, no intrinsics). CI runs on Linux, macOS and Windows; the Windows job builds but does not run the tests. One open, unconfirmed wasm32 lookup bug report (#198).
integration.thread_safety: not documented. Lookups are const member functions that write nothing, so concurrent reads of a const or constexpr container are safe, as with any const object. Value writes on a mutable (constinit) map need external synchronization.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the lookup API matches (find/at/count/contains/equal_range, pair<const K, V> iteration), but: N is a template parameter; there is no insert, erase, operator[], rehash or allocator; hashers are frozen's seeded elsa<T>(value, seed), not std::hash; string keys must be frozen::string, or std::string_view after including <frozen/bits/elsa_std.h>.

gotchas: Duplicate keys are not reliably caught. The Step 1.5 check in bits/pmh.h compares items[0] with items[i] rather than with the members of each bucket, so most duplicates make the seed search spin. Under constexpr that shows up as a constexpr step-limit error; a map built at runtime loops forever (#181).

A map that is neither constexpr nor constinit may be built at runtime, with the seed search running at static-init or first use. Use constinit (C++20), as examples/value_modification.cpp does, to force compile-time construction and get an error when it fails.

There is no operator[]. at() throws std::out_of_range, or calls std::abort when exceptions are off. Custom hashers must accept a seed and should be close to pairwise-independent; a weak hash does not break correctness but makes compiles slow or exceed constexpr limits.

The default key type frozen::string is a non-owning pointer+length view. std::string_view keys work only if you include the internal header frozen/bits/elsa_std.h, which the README does not mention. The version macros read 1.1.1 and the CMake project reads 1.1.0, while the latest tag is 1.2.0.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick frozen over ConstexprCore/perfect_hash or constexpr-phf (Kronuz) when you want the long-established, C++14-compatible option with a full std-like container family, including ordered map/set with lower_bound. Pick those (or static_maps) when lookup throughput matters most: ConstexprCore's benchmark has frozen::unordered_map at 0.16 vs 1.08 billion queries/s. Unlike the gperf-style generators (triehash, strager/perfect-hash-tables), frozen needs no external build step.
verified_claims_summary: The static_maps preprint (arXiv 2602.22506) timed construction plus lookup for frozen::unordered_map (frozen::basic_string keys, built at compile time) against std::unordered_map<std::string_view> (libstdc++, built at runtime inside the timed region). Setup: g++ 15.2.1 -O3 -march=native on a Core i5-1240P laptop. Results: 44.9 vs 89.6 us for 1,024 individually timed lookups in an 84-key map (~2.0x); 1365.5 vs 1746.8 us translating 65,536 codons through a 64-key map (~1.28x); 15804.5 vs 21228.1 us for 258,688 value updates in a 4,042-key map (~1.34x).
status_note: The README says the library is in maintenance mode: it still merges cleanups (last commit 2026-09-23; 1.2.0 tagged 2024-06). It is Apache-2.0 and header-only, so you can copy include/frozen into your tree or install via CMake.
